question: Explain why a radial magnetic field is used in a moving coil galvanometer. How does it make the deflection directly proportional to the current?

options.A: In a radial magnetic field, the normal to the coil remains perpendicular to $\vec B$, so $\sin\theta=1$ for all deflections. Hence $NIAB=k\phi$ and $\phi=\dfrac{NAB}{k}I$, making the scale linear.
options.B: A radial magnetic field makes the plane of the coil perpendicular to $\vec B$ at all times, so $\sin\theta=0$ and no deflection occurs.
options.C: A radial magnetic field reduces the restoring torque to zero, so the deflection is independent of current.
options.D: A radial magnetic field is used only to increase coil resistance; it does not affect the torque-current relation.
